A_target.statement:
Let $\phi: \R \to \R$ be [[Definition:Convex Real Function|convex]] and $X$ an [[Definition:Integrable Function|integrable]] [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] with $\map \phi X$ integrable.
Then:
:$\map \phi {\expect X} \le \expect {\map \phi X}$

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi$ be [[Definition:Convex Real Function|convex]] and $a \in \R$.
Then there exists $m \in \R$ such that:
:$\forall x \in \R: \map \phi x \ge \map \phi a + m \paren {x - a}$

derived.E[L(X)] = phi(E[X]): because L is affine and E[X - E[X]] = 0

object_map.reformulation: Replace the convex function by its supporting line at the mean, reducing the inequality to linearity of expectation.

validity_conditions: phi convex guarantees a supporting line at a = E[X] lying below phi everywhere.
Taking expectations of phi(X) >= L(X) preserves the inequality (monotonicity).
E[L(X)] = phi(E[X]) because the affine part has mean-zero argument.
proof_plan: Let $a = \expect X$ and let $\map L x = \map \phi a + m \paren {x - a}$ be a [[Definition:Supporting Line|supporting line]] of $\phi$ at $a$.

By [[Expectation is Monotone|monotonicity of expectation]]:
:$\expect {\map \phi X} \ge \expect {\map L X}$

By [[Expectation is Linear|linearity]]:
:$\expect {\map L X} = \map \phi a + m \paren {\expect X - a} = \map \phi {\expect X}$
Hence:
:$\map \phi {\expect X} \le \expect {\map \phi X}$
{{qed}}
